item.desc: Watching this series—of which this video is Part 2—you might come away thinking there are a LOT of things that bother me about living in China. But honestly, that couldn’t be further from the truth. Overall, I absolutely love living here. Most of the things we talk about are simply cultural differences or minor frustrations that, after 16 years in China, I barely even notice in everyday life anymore. My experience here as a foreigner has been overwhelmingly positive, and a huge part of that comes down to the people. The vast majority of Chinese people I’ve met over the years have been incredibly kind, friendly and welcoming—and that’s one of the biggest reasons China has felt like home for so long. But I also think that genuinely loving a place means being able to talk honestly about it. I don’t want my videos to present China as either the perfect country some people imagine it to be, or the terrible place others insist it is. Neither reflects the China I’ve actually experienced. Like anywhere else, there are things I love, things I don’t understand, things that frustrate me, and occasionally things I genuinely believe could and should improve. So this series isn’t about complaining about China. It’s about sharing a more complete picture of what living here for 16 years has actually been like—the good, the bad, the funny, the frustrating and everything in between. Some of these things are simply cultural differences that I’ve learned to accept. Others are things I genuinely think are worth talking about. And for those of you watching from outside China, perhaps some of them will also give you a better idea of what to expect if you ever come here yourself. After 16 years, China is home to me. And I think being honest about your home—including its imperfections—is far more meaningful than pretending everything about it is perfect.
